historical_anchor: On 14 Jun Oldendorf's older battleships/cruisers/destroyers moved close to Saipan/Tinian and delivered more methodical shore bombardment than Lee's fast battleships had on 13 Jun.
Historical coastal batteries damaged California and Tennessee and a destroyer; most deep beach defenses nevertheless survived into D-Day.

branch_execution.close_fire_support: Seven old battleships with cruisers/destroyers conduct methodical target-by-target fire. Branch Japanese prior warning/concealment reduces target exposure but cannot prevent close-range suppression and destruction of visible guns/AA positions.
branch_execution.UDT_minesweep: Beach/reef reconnaissance, minesweeping and obstacle work continue and make the 15 Jun landing geometry unambiguous.
branch_execution.carrier_air: TF58 maintains rotating runway/C2/gun/aircraft suppression while part of the carrier force refuels/rearms.

additional_defense_effect.interpretation: This is additional 14 Jun damage/suppression, not cumulative destruction of all defenses. Deep caves, reverse-slope positions and many beach weapons survive.

US_surface_damage.CALIFORNIA: Moderate local damage from coastal fire; air-search/radar function temporarily degraded but no campaign-out.
US_surface_damage.TENNESSEE: Light-to-moderate coastal-fire damage; remains in fire-support mission.
US_surface_damage.destroyer_screen: One destroyer receives light/moderate coastal-fire damage; remains operational or short local repair only.
